output.summary: The record FY2026 result is mostly a commodity price effect. Revenue rose 46.5%, bushels fell 0.9%, handling revenue was flat, and the cooperative ranks mid-pack against peers who adopted no comparable program. The 6% cost-per-bushel gain comes entirely from maintenance cut from 2.8 to 1.9 cents. Deferred work orders have tripled. Harlan Junction has a real dust and ignition hazard: the insurer's findings, a near-miss closed without the SP-04 investigation, and a disconnected sensor. Drying and grading knowledge sits with one person near retirement. The expansion case assumes peak prices, while the outlook shows prices falling back. Fix the hazards, capture the knowledge, and defer the vote until the case is rebuilt. Q1 to Q3 would test the remaining uncertainties.
